title: result
description: The structured result a worker session returns (BRIEF 9.4), passed to claude -p as --json-schema and re-validated in code.

provenance.description: a path with a locator the manifest can resolve

heading.description: a finding is a Results passage: the Results heading it stands under, naming the question; reuse one the section already has when it fits (the ticket's title when absent)

replaces.description: the id of the finding this one replaces, when it narrows or corrects it (a scope-down), or of the inherited Results passage (P<n>) it checks; null otherwise

evidence.description: when it replaces an inherited claim: whether this project's evidence supports, narrows, or contradicts it

reason.description: when it replaces an owner's passage (P<n>): one sentence on why its evidence, its provenance, overrides the owner's text; required then

passages.description: what this ticket adds to the paper's sections (Introduction, Discussion, Methods, References), each written by code into research/sections/; Results is written as findings. A claim sentence ends with its provenance tag, and math is LaTeX ($...$, $$...$$)

heading.description: the heading it stands under; reuse one the section already has when it fits

text.description: Markdown, from one claim to a paragraph

replaces.description: the id of the passage this one replaces (P<n>), or null

evidence.description: when it replaces an inherited claim: whether this project's evidence supports, narrows, or contradicts it

reason.description: when it replaces an owner's passage: one sentence on why its evidence overrides the owner's text; required then, and the passage carries that evidence as a res, ref, or code tag

references.description: every work the ticket drew on, each by a DOI, an arXiv id, or its exact title (never a URL, which is never looked up), with a note kept on its dossier under the ticket's id and never read by the scout; acceptance looks up each one no dossier holds yet (decision 17; ticket 98)

identifier.description: a DOI, an arXiv id, or the work's exact title; never a URL

note.description: what the ticket drew on the work for; may be empty

parameters.description: the rule from code to Methods: a one-sentence reason for every parameter your change to code/ sets away from its default, every default a method you add or change gives itself, and every sensitive default you leave unset (a random draw no seed fixes, a solver at its default tolerances); also any value the code does not show (read from a config file, say), with its value. Code fills each value and default it can see; the verifier judges the reasons

method.description: the method the parameter belongs to: the function or the library call, as the code names it

name.description: the parameter's name as the code or the library spells it

value.description: the value, only for one the code does not show; code fills the rest

default.description: filled by code: the default, "not checked" until the project's environment is installed, "unseeded", or null for a method's own default

path.description: filled by code: the file the parameter is set in

line.description: filled by code: the line it is set on

not_methods.description: the rule from code to Methods: functions your change to code/ adds or changes that are not methods the paper should describe and that code does not already take for plumbing; the verifier judges each

name.description: the function as the code names it, or code/<path>#<function>

why.description: one sentence: why it is not a method

touches.description: the touch set the proposed ticket would take; used by admission's duplicate check (ticket 37)

jobs.description: experiment tickets: the job ids a running result leaves for the poller

blocked_on.description: what blocks the ticket; a verification that lacks material it needs says `material <code|data|software>: <the item>` (decision 17; ticket 97), and the owner or the decider is asked about it

verification.description: a verification ticket's verdict on its inherited result (decision 17; ticket 97): the route it took; its findings replace the result's inherited claims, each saying in `evidence` whether this project's evidence supports, narrows, or contradicts it

route.description: reproduced: the project's own code at the commit intake recorded, changed only to run here; ported: the same logic in another language or runtime; reimplemented: written from the inherited Methods. A read of a cited claim's reference is code's, through the consultant

commit.description: for reproduced: the commit intake recorded, which the run used; null otherwise

substitute.description: the substitute data the verdict was reached on, when the inherited data was not used; every finding then narrows its claim to that data
